blocks.text: Imagine you're a detective trying to decipher a secret code. In computer systems, the 'code' is the instruction set architecture (ISA), which defines how software communicates with hardware.

blocks.markdown: The Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) serves as the interface between software and hardware. It defines the set of instructions that a processor can execute, including their binary encoding, the data types they operate on, and the addressing modes used to access data.

blocks.title: Instruction Set Architecture (ISA)
blocks.text: ISA is the part of the processor that is visible to the programmer or compiler writer. It includes the instruction set, word size, memory address modes, processor registers, and data types.

blocks.markdown: At the heart of an ISA is the instruction encoding. Each instruction is represented in binary and consists of several fields, typically including an opcode and operands. The opcode specifies the operation to be performed, while operands indicate the data to be used.

blocks.title: Instruction Encoding
blocks.text: An instruction encoding typically includes an opcode field and one or more operand fields. The opcode determines the operation, and the operands specify the data.

blocks.title: Example of Instruction Encoding
blocks.prompt: Consider a simple instruction format with a 4-bit opcode and two 4-bit operands. How would the instruction 'ADD R1, R2' be encoded?

steps.text: Register R1 is encoded as 0001 and R2 as 0010.

blocks.answer: The instruction 'ADD R1, R2' is encoded as 0001 0001 0010.

blocks.markdown: Addressing modes define how the operands of an instruction are accessed. Common addressing modes include register, immediate, and memory addressing.

rows: Operands are constants within the instruction
blocks.caption: Comparison of Addressing Modes

blocks.title: Addressing Mode Example
blocks.prompt: How does the immediate addressing mode differ from the register addressing mode in terms of instruction execution?

steps.text: In immediate addressing, the operand is a constant value encoded directly in the instruction.
In register addressing, the operand is located in a register, requiring a register lookup.

blocks.answer: Immediate addressing uses constant values directly, while register addressing requires accessing data from registers.

blocks.title: ISA Guarantees
blocks.text: An ISA guarantees a consistent set of instructions and addressing modes that a compiler can rely on to generate machine code.

blocks.markdown: The distinction between RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computer) and CISC (Complex Instruction Set Computer) architectures is also part of the ISA discussion. RISC architectures focus on a small set of simple instructions, while CISC architectures have a larger set of more complex instructions.

points: ISAs define the set of instructions and addressing modes available to a processor.
Instruction encoding typically includes an opcode and operand fields.
Addressing modes determine how operands are accessed in instructions.
RISC and CISC represent different philosophies in ISA design.
